questiontext.text: What best describes an array of objects?

answer.text: A. A collection of primitive data types of the same kind

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — primitives are not objects.

answer.text: B. A collection of class instances stored under one variable name

feedback.text: ✅ Correct — An array of objects stores multiple instances of a class (e.g. Product[]).

answer.text: C. A collection of unrelated variables

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — arrays hold elements of one consistent type.

answer.text: D. A collection that can change its size automatically

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — arrays in Java have a fixed length.

questiontext.text: In private Product[] products;, what does Product represent?

answer.text: A. A field name

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — products is the field name, not Product.

answer.text: B. A method

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — not a method declaration.

answer.text: C. The object type stored in the array

feedback.text: ✅ Correct — Product is the class type of each element in the array.

answer.text: D. The array variable

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — products is the variable, not the type.

answer.text: A. Ten Product objects are created automatically

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — Java doesn’t auto-create the contained objects.

answer.text: B. The array reference is created, but its elements are null

feedback.text: ✅ Correct — The constructor creates an array of references but no Product objects yet.

answer.text: C. The array and all Product objects are initialised

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — only the array structure exists.

answer.text: D. The Store cannot hold any products yet

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — the Store can hold products; it’s just empty.

answer.text: A. To print all products

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — printing is done by listProducts().

answer.text: B. To return true when the array is full

feedback.text: ✅ Correct — It checks if total equals the array length.

answer.text: C. To count how many products have been added

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — total itself counts products.

answer.text: D. To check whether a specific product exists

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — it doesn’t search for an item.

questiontext.text:
Which line correctly adds a Product object to the Store?
(As shown in the lecture slides — add() takes a Product object as a parameter.)

answer.text: A. store.addProduct(productName, code);

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — wrong parameters; add() doesn’t take primitives directly.

answer.text: B. store.add(new Product("TV", 1234, 899.99, true));

feedback.text: ✅ Correct — This matches the lecture code, where add() receives a Product object.

answer.text: C. store.products.add(product);

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — products is a private array, not a List.

answer.text: D. products.add(product);

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — same reason, not accessible outside Store.

answer.text: A. The number of products in the store

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — total stores that count, not return value.

answer.text: B. Nothing (void)

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — method has a boolean return type.

answer.text: C. A boolean showing if the add succeeded

feedback.text: ✅ Correct — It returns true if added successfully and false if full.

answer.text: D. The newly added Product

feedback.text: ❌ Incorrect — doesn’t return the Product itself.
